decisions.reason: A niche citrus crate that is only mentioned on the website gives weak evidence against aspirations, but a large firm's slack lets it carry the product for another year before problemistic search would justify dropping it.
Having its own page signals that management is investing in this foldable large container, which fits the firm's core returnable-packaging business, so there is no shortfall that calls for search.
A stackable plastic crate is a core, low-risk extension of the established business and should perform close to the firm's historical aspiration levels.
A medium-duty rackable pallet extends the pallet range with low incremental cost, and with only a brief mention so far, slack allows it to be kept while results remain uncertain.
Spill-retention pallets serve regulation-driven demand with steady margins, and the dedicated page shows the firm is committed to the product.
The pallet with load retainers is featured prominently and fits the core pallet line, so it is likely meeting aspirations and gives no reason to reallocate resources.
